headline: Best-ever quarterly profit on surging tanker rates
summary_short: Frontline reported Q2 2026 revenue of $943.3M (+32.1% q/q, +96.5% y/y) and net profit of $659.2M ($2.96/share), its best quarterly profit ever.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $943.3M on higher spot TCE rates across all vessel classes (VLCC $152,700/day, Suezmax $111,500/day, LR2/Aframax $92,400/day, all up sharply q/q). Adjusted profit of $580.2M was driven primarily by TCE earnings rising from $536.5M to $753.3M q/q. The company declared a $2.61/share dividend and plans a further $0.80/share special dividend tied to two VLCC sales. Weighted average financing margin fell 52bps to 126bps via refinancing. No formal forward guidance beyond Q3 contracted TCE rates was given.
confidence_notes: Figures are IFRS as filed by this foreign private issuer (6-K), not US GAAP. Adjusted profit and TCE are company-defined non-GAAP measures reconciled in the release's Appendix I.

drivers.explanation: Increase versus the prior quarter was primarily driven by higher TCE earnings, which increased from $536.5 million to $753.3 million in the second quarter.
Tanker utilization was supported by Middle East and Red Sea disruption rerouting trade around the Cape of Good Hope and rising US/Brazil crude exports lengthening voyages.
Includes a $54.7 million gain on sale of two Suezmax tankers delivered in the quarter, one of several non-recurring items added back to reach adjusted profit.
